compiled_state.title: As a DSO contributor, I want a dogfooding fixture suite verifying the linter blocks violation files and passes clean files, so that enforcement correctness is continuously verified.
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Ships the end-to-end dogfooding fixture suite under plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/design-md/.
**Why**: Enforcement correctness must be continuously verified against known-good and known-bad fixture files across all scope-eligible file families.
**Scope**:
- IN: Violation fixture files (one per violation class), clean fixture files (one per scope-eligible file family), fixture verification test, latency recording
- OUT: Lint wrapper implementation (draft-2), Sprint Phase F integration (draft-4)

## Done Definitions

- plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/design-md/ exists and contains at least one violation file per violation class (hardcoded hex/rgb, off-scale spacing, off-scale font-size, broken token ref, WCAG-failing fg/bg) ← Satisfies: sc-6 (sc-6: "End-to-end dogfooding fixture verification at closure")
  ← Validates Closure Check: "The directory plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/design-md/ exists and contains at least one violation file and at least one clean file per scope-eligible file family."
- plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/design-md/ contains at least one clean file per scope-eligible file family (CSS, SCSS, TSX, JSX, Vue, Svelte, HTML, SSR templates) ← Satisfies: sc-6
- design-md-lint.sh blocks on each violation file and passes on each clean file when executed against the fixture directory ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Cold-start and warm-cache wall-clock latency are recorded in the closure log; cold-start exceeding 30s emits a documented advisory ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Coverage] Each violation class must be represented by a distinct fixture file to ensure the linter's violation detection is granular, not a single catch-all.
- [Latency] Cold-start latency depends on npx download time; the 30s advisory threshold is documenting latency expectations, not a hard failure.
- [Maintenance] Fixture files should be minimal — just enough to trigger or avoid the specific violation class — to reduce maintenance burden when the linter evolves.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
